title: The Permutohedron Paradigm: Every Possible Order
description:
The Permutohedron Paradigm: Every Possible Order is Book Seven (Fire) of The Five Orders of Space, by DICTO. It follows one move, two neighbouring values changing places, from a hexagon through four-dimensional scutoid tissues to a family of solids and back to the bells, in an Opening, fifteen chapters in five parts and an Epilogue.

Opening, One Swap: three bells, one swap of neighbours at a time, draw a hexagon. Part One, The swap builds solids. Chapter 1, Orderings of Three: the Truncated Triangle: every truncated triangle is the permutohedron of three values, and every 2-dimensional face of every permutohedron is a truncated triangle or a rectangle (#88, #20). Chapter 2, Orderings of Four: Kelvin's Cell: the 24 orders of four values, joined by 36 swaps of three kinds, are Kelvin's cell, the one permutohedron that fills space alone (#100, #26). Chapter 3, The Slider and Its Silent Station: the permutohedra of four symmetrically spaced values are the solids of DICTONIC's golden loop; each fills space with its reciprocal in one way only, and at the golden stop the fourth harmonic falls silent (#48, #105, #94). Chapter 4, The Bonds as Spacing: the weight that drives the web of bonds is the relative difference of the gaps, d = (g − m)/(g + m) (#52, #53). Chapter 5, Where the Paradigm Stops: the RD Taken Apart: fourteen half rhombic dodecahedra close into the chamfered cube, a zonohedron that is not a permutohedron, and with cube pyramids it fills space (exact).

Part Two, Swaps inside cells: scutoid tissues. Chapter 6, Scutoids in Three Dimensions: flat-faced scutoid shells, their polar flip and the cycle that fills space. Chapter 7, Five Values: the Web of Swaps and Its Vacuus: the 120 orderings of five values, the 65 central slices of the 4D permutohedron with five DICTO 1:2 Truncated Octahedra at its heart, and the Mirror Law (#105, #107). Chapter 8, Centre I. The 4D Permutohedron Swept: a Scutoid Tissue: 26 births, 66 swaps and 26 deaths, counted by the Eulerian numbers (#104). Chapter 9, Centre II. Every Simple 4-Polytope Is a Scutoid Tissue: every simple 4-polytope, swept, is a scutoid tissue counted by its h-vector; between the 600-cell and the 120-cell the swaps balance, 601 each way (#104, #108). Chapter 10, Rosettes: Many Neighbours Swapping at Once: which uniform 4-polytopes sweep as clean tissues and which only in rosettes, read from the Coxeter chain; rosettes balance by symmetry and not without it. Chapter 11, 4D Scutoids: the Swap Rule and Its Walls: the Swap Rule of close packing below s = 1/4, a computer-assisted exact proof stacking by stacking, its walls as swaps one dimension up and straight as sections of a secondary fan (#104, #61).

Part Three, Swaps in every dimension. Chapter 12, Every Number of Values: the central slices and the sweep of the permutohedron of n values counted in every dimension. Chapter 13, The Golden Slice: cutting the 4D permutohedron filling in the golden direction gives a filling of space by cells of exactly 35 kinds, repeating along a plane and never in a third direction, in endlessly many shapes; its window version has 60 tile shapes. Part Four, The summit. Chapter 14, The Permutohedron Family: slide the walls of the permutohedron without turning them and every edge stays a swap: one cone of shapes from Kelvin's cell to the associahedron, whose canonical form is a scattering amplitude; in three dimensions the members that fill space by translation are Fedorov's five parallelohedra, the graphical zonotopes of the connected graphs on four vertices (#49, #50, #89). Part Five, The return. Chapter 15, Change, Rhythm, Harmony: ringers may only swap neighbours, so every extent is a tour of a permutohedron; on four bells there are exactly 5396 extents, and the three principles of Kyushindo (#43) are read off the tours exactly.

Epilogue, What has been shown: the conclusion, open problems and every main claim with its status (proved, exact, computer-assisted, numerical or open). Appendix: the studies, scripts and commits behind each chapter's checks; papers referred to; references; index.

111 pages. Cover by DICTO: the 4D permutohedron, the 120 orderings of five, exploded into its 30 cells, 10 permutohedra in gold and 20 hexagonal prisms in pink (Schlegel view, exact coordinates). Computation, verification and drafting with Claude (Anthropic). Licence CC BY-SA 4.0. More at dictospheres.com.
